chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, he said:

I said to Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام: A woman sees blood for three days or four. He said: She leaves the salat. I said: Then she sees purity for three days or four days. He said: She performs salat. I said: Then she sees blood for three days or four days. He said: She leaves the salat. I said: Then she sees purity for three days or four days. He said: She performs salat. I said: Then she sees blood for three days or four days. He said: She leaves the salat; she does that for what is between that and a month. Then if it stops from her, otherwise she is in the position of the mustahadah.

key_terms.الدَّمَ: blood seen by the woman in the ruling being discussed
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat that is left during bleeding and performed during purity
key_terms.الطُّهْرَ: the state of purity between periods of bleeding
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: a woman experiencing irregular non-menstrual bleeding, treated under a different legal ruling
key_terms.شَهْرٍ: the one-month period up to which this pattern is observed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a woman alternates between bleeding and purity every few days?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for a woman whose bleeding and purity alternate in intervals of three or four days. The Imam عليه السلام states that she leaves salat during the days of blood, performs salat during the days of purity, and continues in this way up to a month; if the bleeding does not stop, she is treated as a mustahadah.
